transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for making time. As part of the normal approval routine for the peer-feedback pilot, I'd like to do a round-robin check-in with the project team member and our HR program partner before I issue the final plan. I want to make sure we're all aligned on the operating safeguards, especially given the tense exchanges that have come up in recent product retrospectives. Before we get into specifics, I'd like to hear from each of you on a couple of things: first, what concerns or risks do you see with running this pilot as currently described, and second, what safeguards do you think we need to have in place to make sure this doesn't replicate the same friction we've been seeing in those retrospective sessions?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Thanks Elena. I'm glad we're doing this check-in before finalizing. I have some concerns about the current pilot description. As it stands, the proposal mentions facilitated discussion, ordinary participation, and a review after the pilot — but it doesn't specify the detailed safeguards, and I think that gap is significant given what's been happening in our retros. I've observed a pattern of dismissive interruptions across our last three retrospectives that's affecting people's willingness to speak openly. I also have specific concerns that some colleagues may not feel safe contributing in a group format at all, and we need to account for that before we put a peer-feedback pilot in front of everyone. Rather than just flag the concern abstractly, I'd like to share exactly what I've observed so we can design the right safeguards. I'd like to reveal that now if it's helpful.

transcript.text: Here's what I've personally observed: across the last three retrospectives, I counted exactly five dismissive interruptions. Additionally, two colleagues who were each affected by those interruptions told me separately that they would only contribute through an anonymous written channel going forward rather than speak up in the group. That's concrete evidence that the current group-only format risks silencing the very people this pilot is meant to include.

transcript.text: Here's the specific HR guidance I confirmed this morning: because this peer-feedback pilot follows repeated conduct concerns, HR has determined four specific requirements that must be incorporated before the final plan is issued. First, the pilot must be opt-in — no one should be required to participate. Second, the facilitator must be an independent neutral facilitator, not someone internal to the team. Third, all participants must sign a written non-retaliation acknowledgment before the pilot begins. And fourth, there must be a documented review exactly 30 days after launch — not just after the pilot ends. This guidance came in after the current draft circulated, which is why it wasn't already reflected in the proposal. I'd strongly recommend we incorporate all four of these into the final plan before Elena issues it.

commitments.detail: Participation is fully opt-in; no one will be required to participate in the peer-feedback pilot.
An independent neutral facilitator external to the team will be engaged to run all pilot sessions.
All participants must sign a written non-retaliation acknowledgment before the pilot begins.
An anonymous written feedback channel will be provided so that colleagues who do not feel safe speaking in a group format can still contribute.
A documented review will occur exactly 30 days after launch, in addition to the end-of-pilot review.
